es.summary: La buprenorfina es un agonista parcial de los receptores mu opioides usado para el manejo de la dependencia a opioides, administrado vía sublingual.
key_points: Agonista parcial: activa parcialmente los receptores mu, reduciendo síntomas de abstinencia.
Se usa en inducción y mantenimiento del tratamiento de dependencia a opioides.
Incluye naloxona en combinaciones para desalentar la inyección intravenosa.
Puede causar depresión respiratoria, especialmente con depresores del SNC.
Se debe monitorizar signos de sobredosis y adherencia al plan de apoyo psicosocial.

mechanism: Se une al receptor mu opioide con alta afinidad pero baja actividad intrínseca.
Bloquea la unión de opioides completos, disminuyendo euforia y síntomas de abstinencia.
En combinaciones, la naloxona no absorbida oralmente actúa si se inyecta, anulando el efecto.
indications: Tratamiento de la dependencia a opioides en adultos.
Inducción y mantenimiento de la terapia de sustitución de opioides.
Uso como parte de un plan integral que incluya consejería y apoyo psicosocial.
contraindications: Hipersensibilidad conocida a la buprenorfina o a cualquiera de sus excipientes.
Uso concomitante de inhibidores potentes de CYP3A4 en pacientes con insuficiencia hepática grave.
Pacientes con depresión respiratoria aguda no controlada.
adverse_effects: Síndrome de abstinencia severa si se interrumpe bruscamente (serio).
interactions: Potenciación de depresión respiratoria con benzodiacepinas, barbitúricos o alcohol.
Inhibidores de CYP3A4 (ej. ketoconazol) aumentan niveles plasmáticos.
Inductores de CYP3A4 (ej. rifampicina) pueden reducir la eficacia.
Medicamentos serotonérgicos pueden aumentar riesgo de síndrome serotoninérgico.
nursing_care: Evaluar alergias, historial de uso de opioides y estado respiratorio antes de administrar.
Monitorizar frecuencia respiratoria, saturación O₂ y nivel de conciencia cada 15‑30 min tras la dosis inicial.
Observar signos de sobredosis: respiración <8/min, somnolencia excesiva, pupilas contraídas.
Retener la dosis y notificar al médico si hay depresión respiratoria o hipotensión marcada.
Registrar la hora y la vía de administración; asegurar que el paciente mantenga el comprimido bajo la lengua hasta disolverse.
patient_teaching: Colocar el comprimido bajo la lengua y no masticar ni tragar durante 30‑60 min.
Evitar comer, beber o fumar durante ese tiempo para asegurar absorción adecuada.
No compartir el medicamento y guardarlo fuera del alcance de niños y mascotas.
Informar sobre los signos de sobredosis y la necesidad de buscar ayuda inmediata.
Mantener citas de consejería y seguir el plan de apoyo psicosocial.
antidote_overdose: Naloxona 0.4‑2 mg IV/IM, repetir cada 2‑3 minutos según respuesta clínica.
Continuar monitorización respiratoria y cardiovascular después de la reversión.

outcomes: Conocimiento del manejo de la medicación: paciente demostrará comprensión del uso correcto de buprenorfina en 2 sesiones educativas.
Seguridad del paciente: paciente no presentará signos de sobredosis durante el periodo de tratamiento.

interventions.action: Evaluar historial de uso de opioides y alergias antes de cada dosis.
interventions.rationale: Identifica factores de riesgo que pueden predisponer a intoxicación.

interventions.action: Monitorizar frecuencia respiratoria y nivel de conciencia cada 30 minutos tras la administración.
interventions.rationale: Detecta precozmente depresión respiratoria, signo de sobredosis.

interventions.action: Enseñar al paciente y familia el procedimiento de administración sublingual y la importancia de no ingerir alimentos inmediatamente.
interventions.rationale: Reduce errores de administración que pueden llevar a toxicidad.

interventions.action: Proveer información escrita sobre signos de sobredosis y cuándo contactar al servicio de urgencias.
interventions.rationale: Facilita la respuesta rápida ante una posible intoxicación.

interventions.action: Mantener naloxona disponible en el área de atención y entrenar al personal en su uso.
interventions.rationale: Permite intervención inmediata en caso de depresión respiratoria grave.

en.summary: Buprenorphine is a partial agonist of mu opioid receptors used for the management of opioid dependence, administered sublingually.
key_points: Partial agonist: partially activates mu receptors, reducing withdrawal symptoms.
Used for induction and maintenance of opioid dependence treatment.
Includes naloxone in combinations to deter intravenous injection.
Can cause respiratory depression, especially with CNS depressants.
Signs of overdose and adherence to psychosocial support plan must be monitored.

mechanism: Binds to the mu opioid receptor with high affinity but low intrinsic activity.
Blocks binding of full opioids, reducing euphoria and withdrawal symptoms.
In combinations, orally absorbed naloxone acts if injected, negating the effect.
indications: Treatment of opioid dependence in adults.
Induction and maintenance of opioid substitution therapy.
Use as part of a comprehensive plan that includes counseling and psychosocial support.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to buprenorphine or any of its excipients.
Concurrent use of potent CYP3A4 inhibitors in patients with severe hepatic impairment.
Patients with uncontrolled acute respiratory depression.
adverse_effects: Severe withdrawal syndrome if abruptly discontinued (serious).
interactions: Potentiation of respiratory depression with benzodiazepines, barbiturates, or alcohol.
CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., ketoconazole) increase plasma levels.
CYP3A4 inducers (e.g., rifampin) may reduce efficacy.
Serotonergic drugs may increase risk of serotonin syndrome.
nursing_care: Assess allergies, opioid use history, and respiratory status before administration.
Monitor respiratory rate, O₂ saturation, and level of consciousness every 15‑30 minutes after the initial dose.
Observe signs of overdose: respiratory rate <8/min, excessive drowsiness, constricted pupils.
Withhold the dose and notify the physician if there is marked respiratory depression or hypotension.
Record the time and route of administration; ensure the patient keeps the tablet under the tongue until dissolved.
patient_teaching: Place the tablet under the tongue and do not chew or swallow for 30‑60 minutes.
Avoid eating, drinking, or smoking during that time to ensure adequate absorption.
Do not share the medication and keep it out of reach of children and pets.
Inform about signs of overdose and the need to seek immediate help.
Maintain counseling appointments and follow the psychosocial support plan.
antidote_overdose: Naloxone 0.4‑2 mg IV/IM, repeat every 2‑3 minutes as clinically indicated.
Continue respiratory and cardiovascular monitoring after reversal.

outcomes: Medication management knowledge: patient will demonstrate understanding of correct buprenorphine use in 2 educational sessions.
Patient safety: patient will not exhibit signs of overdose during the treatment period.

interventions.action: Assess opioid use history and allergies before each dose.
interventions.rationale: Identifies risk factors that may predispose to intoxication.

interventions.action: Monitor respiratory rate and level of consciousness every 30 minutes after administration.
interventions.rationale: Detects early respiratory depression, a sign of overdose.

interventions.action: Teach the patient and family the sublingual administration procedure and the importance of not ingesting food immediately.
interventions.rationale: Reduces administration errors that can lead to toxicity.

interventions.action: Provide written information on overdose signs and when to contact emergency services.
interventions.rationale: Facilitates rapid response to a potential intoxication.

interventions.action: Keep naloxone available in the care area and train staff in its use.
interventions.rationale: Allows immediate intervention in case of severe respiratory depression.

summary.0.quote: Buprenorphine is a partial agonist at the mu-opioid receptor and chronic administration produces physical dependence of the opioid type, characterized by withdrawal signs and symptoms upon abrupt discontinuation or rapid taper.

key_points.2.quote: The inclusion of naloxone with oral preparations of buprenorphine may seem nonsensical given that naloxone has poor oral bioavailability, but this is done to discourage intravenous abuse of buprenorphine, as the naloxone would cancel out the euphoric effects of buprenorphine upon injection.

key_points.3.quote: Warn patients of the potential danger of self-administration of benzodiazepines or other CNS depressants while under treatment with buprenorphine sublingual tablets.

sections.indications.0.quote: Buprenorphine sublingual tablet is a prescription medicine used to treat opioid addiction in adults and is part of a complete treatment program that also includes counseling and behavioral therapy.

sections.indications.2.quote: Buprenorphine sublingual tablet should be used as part of a complete treatment plan that includes counseling and psychosocial support.

sections.adverse_effects.3.quote: • Respiratory and CNS Depression [see Warnings and Precautions (5.2, 5.3)]

sections.adverse_effects.5.quote: Opioid withdrawal occurs in clients using opioids for a chronic period who have abruptly discontinued the drug, or from rapid reversal of the drug’s effect with an opioid antagonist (e.g., naloxone).

sections.interactions.0.quote: Due to additive pharmacologic effects, the concomitant use of benzodiazepines or other CNS depressants, including alcohol, increases the risk of respiratory depression, profound sedation, coma, and death.

sections.interactions.2.quote: The concomitant use of buprenorphine and CYP3A4 inducers can decrease the plasma concentration of buprenorphine [see Clinical Pharmacology (12.3)] , potentially resulting in decreased efficacy or onset of a withdrawal syndrome in patients who have developed physical dependence to buprenorphine.

sections.interactions.3.quote: Serotonin syndrome : Cases of serotonin syndrome, a potentially life-threatening condition, have been reported during concomitant use of opioids with serotonergic drugs.

sections.patient_teaching.4.quote: Buprenorphine sublingual tablet should be used as part of a complete treatment plan to include counseling and psychosocial support.
